prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Production pixel-art asset, genuinely transparent background. Image1 is the AUTHORITATIVE wood, caps, nail heads and shading style. Image2 is the old north-south fence module that needs a clearer replacement. Draw ONE north-south wooden fence module, full object only, no sheet or text.
The fence follows a straight VERTICAL line on the ground in a top-down cozy RPG, with upper/north and lower/south rail ends. It must be visibly a FENCE, not just a tall post. A sturdy capped timber post at the center of the segment, with TWO long rails at waist and knee heights extending from it toward BOTH north and south neighboring segments. Reveal the broad wood faces of the rails on the camera-left side of the center post so the rails remain visible beside and beyond the post. The upper and lower rail runs are offset in HEIGHT (like the horizontal reference), with visible transparent openings rather than one solid stick. Use a mildly oblique elevated view that shows top faces and a side face, but the rail joining endpoints must stay on a single screen-vertical axis. No sideways turn, no diagonal fence across the ground.
Keep the same chamfered golden cap, chestnut wood grain, dark edge shading and small iron nail heads as the atlas. Center post and near/far parts must retain the SAME thickness and waist-height proportions as the horizontal reference. One narrow vertical module: visible width around25-30% of its height, designed to reduce to20x80 pixels inside a40x100 pixel cell. Near/south joining point at bottom, far/north joining point40 native pixels above it. Clean bold pixel clusters and warm shading, no halos, strays or ground.
Center the complete module on a transparent portrait canvas, fully visible without cropping. No floor, grass, ground shadow, border, labels, extra standalone pieces or black background.
